notes: THREE PATCHES IN ONE ZIP, NONE OF THEM PUSHED. v1.10.1.1, .2 and .3 ship together. SERVER RESTART REQUIRED for .3 (it adds a table); .1 and .2 are client only. (1.10.1.1) THE CIRCUIT WAS SEALED AGAINST A PASSAGE THE SERVER HAD OPEN. galaxy.js is lazy loaded on the first galactic tab click and the init message carrying wormholeOpen/reachOpen arrives on socket connect, always earlier, so the setters core.js calls at init did not exist and the server's answer was discarded every load. core.js banks it in window._PASSAGE_SEED unconditionally; galaxy.js seeds from it at load. (1.10.1.2) A REFRESH RAISED UNREAD BADGES FOR MESSAGES NOBODY HAD SENT. addChat took one parameter while chat_history had always called it as addChat(m, true), so the history flag went nowhere and every refresh walked thirty minutes of traffic through the live path. Separately the badge counted ANY message on a non-active channel. Badges are mentions only now, via one predicate the highlight and the sound also read. (1.10.1.3) AND THEN MENTIONS PERSIST. NEW TABLE chat_mentions, created at boot by initDB - an inbox row per mention rather than a read cursor, because the chat rings are count-bounded at 200 per room and a cursor goes wrong the moment the scrollback it measures against is gone. Recorded on the SEND path from the text that shipped, gated on whether the RECIPIENT can read the channel, self-mentions skipped, capped at 5 rows and 12 name lookups per message. Counts are pushed on connect and on each new mention; the client paints them and marks a channel read when its tab is opened. Seen rows are pruned after 30 days, at boot and daily. tools/chat-check.mjs 45 assertions, the predicate, the parser and the inbox all DRIVEN - the inbox against a real in-memory SQLite database using the DDL lifted from db.js. That section needs Node 22.5+ for node:sqlite and prints the NOT RUN banner rather than a pass if it is missing. DEPLOY STATE: v1.10.1.0 IS LIVE on the VPS, confirmed by Jacob directly rather than read off the server. Its notes and CHANGELOG/MANIFEST entries were written before that deploy and read as a pre-deploy checklist; they are marked corrected in place rather than rewritten. Whether the player_cargo migration ran clean is still unverified: SELECT colony_id, COUNT(*) FROM player_cargo GROUP BY colony_id. (1.10.1.4) CHAT MESSAGE LENGTH AND WALL-OF-TEXT SPAM. The cap moves from 240 CHARACTERS to 534 WORDS, roughly 3,200 characters, about 13x. Enforced server side on chat AND whisper, REFUSED rather than truncated, with a 6,000 character ceiling underneath because 534 words says nothing about how long a word may be. A live counter appears in the input from three quarters of the cap, ambers at 90 percent and reds over, and the send button disables; an over-length message is refused WITHOUT clearing the input. Client and server count words with the same expression. AUTO-DUNCE: three messages at or above 481 words (90 percent of the cap) within 60 SECONDS. The window and the sub-cap floor are additions to 'back to back' and both are deliberate - consecutive with no clock dunces a lore writer posting across an evening, and an exact-534 test catches almost nobody. Any ordinary message resets the run. Devs, admins and the owner are exempt. Logged to admins as dunce_auto and reversible with the existing undunce. *** THE CONNECT PAYLOAD, NOW BOUNDED BY THE WEEKLY WIPE IN 1.10.1.5 BUT STILL WORTH A DECISION. *** getChatHistory flattens every ring into ONE JSON frame sent on every connect. At 200 messages per room across ~20 rooms that is ~1.6MB today and ~12MB once messages can be 13x longer. Nothing in this patch changes CHAT_RING_MAX or the payload, so that growth is real and unmitigated. Jacob's call: lower CHAT_RING_MAX, cap the history by bytes, or send only the active room. (1.10.1.5) CHAT CLEARS WEEKLY ON THE TAX DAY BOUNDARY: Sunday 12:00 America/Los_Angeles, the same instant runWeeklyTaxAssessment fires, read from the same _frsMostRecentSundayNoonLA helper. IT SHARES THE BOUNDARY AND NOT THE SCHEDULER, deliberately: frsScheduleTick returns early when FRS is disabled and FRS ships DORMANT, so a wipe folded in there would silently never fire. Own tick, own city_kv marker (chat_wipe_ts) so a server down across noon on Sunday wipes when it returns rather than skipping the week. An UNSET marker records the boundary and waits rather than wiping, so a fresh DB or the first boot after this ships does not clear a chat nobody has had a cycle to fill. Clears the in-memory rings, the chat_log table, and unread mentions older than the boundary - a badge outliving its message is a notification a player cannot resolve by reading. Broadcasts chat_cleared; connected clients empty their panes and show a closing line rather than holding a week the server has forgotten. This also BOUNDS the connect payload noted above: the history can now only hold one week rather than growing without limit, though the ring cap and the single-frame shape are unchanged and a busy week can still fill 200 messages per room. chat-check 68 -> 88, with the boundary driven across both DST transitions and the wipe driven against a real database.
